utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, good afternoon, everybody. Madam Registrar, could you call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. This is case number IT-05-88-T, the Prosecutor versus Vujadin Popovic et al.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, ma'am. For the record all the accused are here. I do not notice any absences on the -- amongst the Defence teams. Prosecution is Mr. McCloskey and Mr. Nicholls. Yes. I understand there are some preliminaries? Yes, Mr. McCloskey?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President, good afternoon. Good afternoon, everyone.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: At this time I would like to make a request, Mr. President, that we take the first three weeks of July as a break. I know that you have issued the -- your decision that we put on witnesses up until the end of June and we've all been planning on what to do with July and hoping to -- that there would be some -- a lawyer appointed for or chosen by General Tolimir and that we would have a better idea. There is nothing that's actually clarified itself on this issue and we are having a very difficult time finding adequate witnesses to fill that time that might not affect the concerns that I think Mr. Bourgon mentioned and that I share with him, that I had mentioned, that we would be getting into issues that may relate to Tolimir. I think most of the Defence counsel have felt the same way, that we need some clarity, if possible, on those three weeks. I can bring in some witnesses but it has been difficult and I think if we are also -- I can tell you we are all very tired as well. This has been ten months of a good pace and as you know, a rigorous case and subject matter but we are ready -- we can put on witnesses in July. We are having trouble but I think it would be a good for all if we took this break. I know that there are efforts to resolve the Tolimir issue. I think OLAD is working hard on that so I hope that will happen soon. But that is just the request I wanted to put forward to you and of course answer any questions you have.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Are there any comments from the Defence teams? Mr. Josse?

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: Well, I only rise, Your Honour, because we were the one team who opposed that suggestion originally. On reflection and on balance, we now support what my learned friend says. So I think the Defence are unanimous in this regard. Of course, it's a matter for the Trial Chamber but I think I would just make that clear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We will be issuing -- thank you, Mr. Josse. We will be issuing a ruling later on today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We've taken note of what you said, Mr. McCloskey. We will not of course pronounce ourselves on your request which seems to have the endorsement of all the Defence teams. We'll need to think about it. In the meantime later on today, we will be handing down a ruling or an order asking you to give -- work on some estimates that would be applicable if there is a joinder, and if not. At the same time, I hope you all understand that the question of joinder as such doesn't hinge necessarily only at the moment -- or the timing of the decision on joinder doesn't hinge necessarily or only on assignment of counsel to Mr. Tolimir. There are various legal issues involved, particularly what has happened in the last ten months or 11 months in his absence, including the hearing of evidence and the tendering of documents. So there are problems ahead, and of course we are - like I would assume you all are - fully aware of. We'll think about your request, Mr. McCloskey, and we'll try to come back to you as soon as we can with a view to making it possible for both sides, if we decide to proceed, to be able to know exactly on what terms and for how long and to what extent. So please allow us to ponder on these issues, and hopefully we'll come back to you very soon. Thank you. Are there any further preliminaries? Yes, Mr. Bourgon?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. President. At this point in time I would like to make an oral application further to information which was provided to us by the Prosecution today. We've received a proofing notes which were drafted by the Prosecution further to their proofing session with Witness 129. Witness 129 is -- will be testifying, not the next witness but the second following witness, and based on the proofing notes that we've received, it appears that there have been some substantial modifications to his -- the information this witness has provided previously to the Prosecution, and this information or the changes, whether new or modified information, goes in the direction of supporting the testimony of the witness who is presently on the stand. And both witnesses are presently in The Hague. The Prosecution has had an opportunity to proof the witness, and the application at this time is to bar any further contact between the Prosecution and the witness. They had the chance to proof him. Now it's better if the witness does not have any contact so that he may testify and not be privy to any further information that this witness presently on the stand might provide to him or not. Of course, on cross-examination, I will raise that issue with the present witness, whether they spoke together, because they are quite close, and this second witness happens to be, as the Chamber will see, the only witness who can corroborate the story put forward by the present witness. Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Actually, this person is one of the two associates that the witness referred to, I take it. What about the second one? Is he also scheduled listed as a witness or not, or isn't he available?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: No. He is not currently scheduled and I don't know if we have a statement from him off the top of my head.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. What's your comment on Mr. Bourgon's request?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I would object. I think this is the subject matter of a previous motion. It seems similar to what they are talking about with Obrenovic so I think some of the law and the facts have been stated there. I don't see any grounds that -- to prevent us from talking to someone unless there is some sort of underlying belief or argument that there is something crooked going on and there is absolutely not. And so I don't, as he has -- as Mr. Bourgon has said, he will be able to cross-examine the witness fully, and I don't see any reason that we wouldn't be speaking to the witness. It would be normal that we would continue to speak. It's Mr. Vanderpuye's witness. I think Mr. Vanderpuye, at this point, is probably finished with most of his proofing so this may not be a big issue but like the Obrenovic issue wasn't, since I never saw Mr. Obrenovic any way but I can find that out, if that would be interesting, maybe we can avoid the whole issue but my guess is Mr. Vanderpuye would have planned to see him today or perhaps tomorrow, but I don't know. I can find that out but I see no grounds for it. I don't see the point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment, Mr. Zivanovic, because Mr. Bourgon was standing before. Already standing before. Yes go ahead, Mr. Bourgon.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President, just briefly in reply first I would like to confirm that the second associate is a Defence witness and the Prosecution has taken a statement from him. Of course, they won't call him because he's not giving the same information. But we will be calling the other -- this other associate. As for the one that is presently scheduled to testify, the Prosecution has met him, so they've had an opportunity to discuss everything they wanted to, and we are not suggesting any impropriety on the part of the Prosecution, although it is a fact that we are seeing from the proofing notes that we've received that this witness is modifying what he previously said in statements, so whether he was prompted to do so in questions by the Prosecution, whether he was -- simply spoke with this witness or whether it is truthful or refreshed -- new recollection on his behalf, whatever the situation, I think it is in the interests of justice to have a witness that is not influenced in any way before he testifies here a couple of days from now. Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But you all know -- I mean, and of course, you amongst the -- foremost amongst others because of where you come from, which jurisdiction you come from, that in a system like we have, where you have proofing, that's why we also have a cross-examination system, and that's what it's all about basically. I mean the control is in the cross-examination. Anyway, we've taken note of your submission, Mr. Bourgon. Mr. McCloskey, if you could kindly verify, as you suggested you could do, and then come back to us, that would help us immensely come to a pristine conclusion on this. Thank you. Mr. Zivanovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. I just like to add that the information report with the conversation of the Prosecution investigators with the second assistant of this witness was disclosed to us under Rule 68.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Which one, the one who is witness 129 or the other one that Mr. Bourgon --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: No, the other assistant.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. So that's it. That's for your information. So I think we can proceed with admitting the witness in the courtroom, unless there are further preliminaries. There seem to be none. Yes, Madam Usher, please. While we are waiting, it occurred to my mind yesterday that you haven't come back to us in a final fashion, manner, on the question of the aerial images. You had told us that there had been some consultations and exchange of correspondence and that you would be coming back to us shortly. Shortly, is of course a relative term in this environment. But if perhaps you could at some point in time come back to us and pinpoint the exact position of where you stand, it would be very helpful.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Acimovic, good afternoon to you and welcome back.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We are going to proceed with your testimony and then we see where we get at the end of today. Mr. Nicholls -- I was going to call you Nikolic.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Once a day is enough. Could we please start in private session. I will try to very quickly wrap up all the parts that need to be there. There is not much more.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Let's go into private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Make sure that this document is not broadcast as we go into open session, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Could we go to private session, please and redact that line.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We will have to redact and go into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I still need to sign the redaction.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay, sir, I'm nearly done with the questions I have for you. I just want to wrap up about how events finished at the school and how you came to leave the school and then we'll be almost done. First of all, during the time at the school, were you able to see whether or not Mr. Popovic was armed, whether he had a weapon?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He had a pistol.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. You spoke about how Popovic called the brigade and requested trucks. Did he ask for anything else from the brigade, for anything else to be sent or anybody to come from the brigade, anything else?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. He said, "Urgently send me one of the two men who were or who were located either in Petkovci or in Orahovac," one of these two locations but I'm not sure which one he actually mentioned.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, at the time did you know who he was referring to?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever learn who these people were who had been requested to be sent to the Rocevic school?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In a subsequent conversation with Milorad Trbic, when I explained to him --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment, one moment. Yes, Mr. Meek?

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: I would ask that the witness take his ear phones off also.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Nicholls? There is a request for submission to be made. Yes go ahead, Mr. Meek.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Can I approach my friend for a minute?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: I'll withdraw the objection at this point, Judge.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Yes. I'll repeat the question myself to you, Mr. Acimovic, and then you start answering it. Did you ever learn who these people were who had been requested to be sent to the Rocevic school? And you had just started telling us, "In a subsequent conversation with Milorad Trbic, when I explained to him --" Will you go on, take it up from there, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] When I explained to him what this was all about, when I told him that Popovic had uttered that sentence, he told me that he had probably meant either him or Jasikovac. That Popovic most probably had referred to either him or Jasikovac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And which Jasikovac is that? Who is Jasikovac? Do you know his first name or his position?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The commander of the military police company.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Of the Zvornik Brigade?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did Mr. Trbic tell you whether he or Mr. Jasikovac had gone to the Rocevic school?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Later on, I learned, and I heard, that Jasikovac had gone down there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. And just to be clear, did you learn that from Mr. Trbic or from somebody else?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I believe that Trbic told me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. Now, can you tell the Court please how you came to leave the school that morning after all this had gone on? How did -- what happened? How did you end up leaving the school and when did you leave?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I told Popovic, as I have already explained in my previous statements, that I had to go back to my unit, given the situation that my unit was in. I told him that I had to go. At that moment he called the brigade and told them exactly what I have just mentioned. He called the brigade, I don't know who he spoke to, and he asked that person to urgently send one of these two men to Rocevic. At that moment he told me to wait until one of the two turned up at the school and only then to go back to my unit. I told him that I wouldn't wait, that I had to leave immediately. He was in a haste. The whole conversation that I conducted with Popovic was carried out in a haste. He rushed me. He came to the door and he ordered me to wait for one of the two to get to the school and only then to leave to go to my unit. And then he went down the corridor swearing and cursing. I shouted after him, "I'm not going to wait. I'm going to leave before." However, he went down the corridor. Whether he left the school or whether he stayed on I'm not sure. A few moments later, or maybe a few minutes later, I decided to leave that place where I was. I went through the school door and I started walking to my car, where my car was parked. I thought that maybe somebody would stop me but nobody did. As nobody stopped me, I got into my car and I returned to my unit, and this would be the long and the short of that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And approximately what time did you get back to your 2nd Battalion headquarters?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot say with any degree of certainty, but I believe that it was in the period between 11.30 and 12.15.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just to be very clear, that's in the afternoon?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's when I left. That's when I left the school, in that interval.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Before you left the school, or when you were leaving the school, did you see whether any prisoners were being transported? Were any prisoners being put on trucks? Any movement of the prisoners going on in any way?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot say for sure whether there were any of them or not. I was in a severe nightmare at the time, so I cannot be 100 per cent sure whether the boarding or the loading of prisoners had already started to one of the trucks. I cannot confirm that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And briefly, what did you do when you got back to the battalion headquarters?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Very briefly, I explained to my colleagues that I mentioned in my previous statement, and informed them about what was going on in the Rocevic school, and what the intentions were, what was going to happen with those prisoners. I explained to them briefly, and I believe that at that point I called them fools or some such-like names. Once again, I called the duty officer in the Zvornik Brigade and while I was calling him I was explaining to them what was happening. I wanted to get in touch again with the chief or possibly with the commander. However, the duty officer told me again what he told me on the previous day, that is to say that neither of the two were at the brigade headquarters. I also explained to the duty officer what was going on in the school, what actions I had taken, and what potentially could happen to those prisoners. In response, he said that he couldn't do anything about it, that he was helpless. That was the context.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, in the answer you just gave you said you explained to my colleagues that I mentioned in my previous statement. Could you tell us who those two colleagues were when you came back and explained what was happening at the Rocevic school?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I remember those were Vujo Lazarevic and Mitar Lazarevic. I asked them to tell me if there was any news or any new developments in the defence area of the battalion, and we were mainly focused on our duties and obligations relating to the unit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Were you ever disciplined in any way or was your failure to follow this order ever discussed? Did you have problems with that refusal to follow this order after these events had finished? And I mean problems from the brigade.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall whether you ever discussed it with any -- with either the Chief of Staff Obrenovic or with any or with the commander or with anybody else what had happened at the Rocevic school?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I didn't have an opportunity to discuss it with the commander and as for the Chief of Staff, on one occasion I raised this subject with him while he was visiting my unit. He said -- actually I tried to ask him whether he had been informed that I tried to call him on numerous times and that I had tried to get in touch with him. He cut short my statement, that conversation, and said that he hadn't been available, that he had been in the field and that he was inaccessible and that he also knew nothing about the events that I was talking about, and that is where he cut the conversation short.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Could I have one moment?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Thank you, I have no further questions at this time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, Mr. Nicholls. Now, before we start with the cross-examinations, can I ask you one by one the estimated time you require? Mr. Zivanovic, you had indicated two hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Meek? You had indicated one hour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Your Honours, I think we had put down 45 minutes and I believe that will be reduced substantially.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Ms. Nikolic or Mr. Bourgon? You indicated two hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: No change to what we indicated, Mr. President, but that will be, of course, adjusted depending on what happens and the way the cross-examination, Mr. Zivanovic does. Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Bourgon. Mr. Lazarevic?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Well, as things stand now we don't have any cross-examination but I cannot exclude the possibility that something might raise. But now we don't have any cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you, Madam Fauveau? You had indicated 30 minutes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, for the moment, we don't expect to have any questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Mr. Krgovic or Mr. Josse?

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: Exactly the same, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. And Mr. Haynes? You had indicated one hour.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: That's very pessimistic. I think 20 or 30 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Who wishes to start? Mr. Zivanovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Acimovic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Acimovic, from your answers, one may conclude, and also on the basis on the information that I have, that as a soldier and as a company commander, and a battalion commander, you were a very brave and courageous man?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is your assessment.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: You don't agree?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I wouldn't like to speak about myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I also have information that you were promoted from a private to a company commander and eventually battalion commander particularly due to what I just mentioned before. Do you not also wish to speak about this?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I would tell you that it is true that I don't have any formal military training and I acquired my rank during the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Zivanovic and Mr. Acimovic, you're racing. And that's no good for the interpreters. Please slow down. You speak the same language, Mr. Acimovic, and Mr. Zivanovic, and there is a tendency when that is the case for overlapping and one doesn't leave -- allow enough time for the interpreters to catch up with you. So please allow a short pause between question and answer. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: From your yesterday's and today's evidence, one may conclude that throughout your military service, you always observed military rules and regulations. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Mainly speaking, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: When you say mainly speaking, yes, does that imply that you did not take part in the commission of any crimes, nor did you allow this to be done by men under your command?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: That also means that you didn't try to conceal these crimes and their perpetrators; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Can you please repeat the question. Or make it more clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Does that also mean that you did not conceal this kind of crimes and their perpetrators?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I didn't conceal them.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell me, please, when were you demobilised?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I believe that it was in 1995 or 1996. I'm not 100 per cent sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: You were living in Rocevici with your family, correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: And as you told us yesterday, two companies of your soldiers were also natives of Rocevici?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: At the time, you were certainly very keen for your family and the families of your soldiers to be safe; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: At any rate, yes, that was the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Let us just please clarify one thing. As a battalion commander, you were directly subordinate to the brigade commander, correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: In July 1995, or more precisely these two days that we are discussing here, when the prisoners were in the school in Rocevici, Dragan Obrenovic was the commander; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I believe it is so because the commander himself was not present at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: In your evidence yesterday, you mentioned that at the time, you didn't have a deputy in your battalion, that also one of your officers was away, I think he was a security officer, and that practically you had two assistants, one was Mitar Lazarevic and the other one was Vujo Lazarevic; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I didn't say that I had only two assistants.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I didn't -- I misunderstood you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I said that I remember that they were there at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell me, what was precisely the duty of Mitar Lazarevic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He was a desk officer for general affairs.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us more precisely what does that involve, a desk officer for general affairs, in a battalion?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Mostly he kept records, paid salaries and things like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Was he also in charge of keeping the records and the archive?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think that the general affairs desk officer kept the archives pending their return to the brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know whether these archives were handed over to the brigade?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: You did not attend the handover?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: What kind of handover?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: The handover of the archives.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That was not one of my duties.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Did he perhaps keep the attendance lists or the presence lists of men in the battalion?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Can you please be more precise? What do you mean by keeping the attendance records in the battalion?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: We had an opportunity to see certain forms, not only coming from your battalion but from other battalions as well, which contain information when personnel were in the unit, when personnel were away on leave, et cetera. I'm asking you whether this was kept by Mitar Lazarevic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I believe that a general affairs officer was not in charge of keeping attendance records. This was mainly within the purview of unit commanders.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: When you say unit commanders, do you refer to company commanders?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: And what was the situation in the battalion command? Who kept those records of attendance?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We had certain assignments and rotas that probably we adhered to. We knew who was on duty, who was supposed to carry out certain activities and things like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Perhaps it will be helpful if I showed you these records just to refresh your memory of how they look like. But I'll do it a little bit later. However I'm under the impression that we are not speaking about the same thing since apparently you cannot remember this form so I'm going to show it to you later on. Can you tell me, please, one more thing? Your battalion had a facility in Kozluk, as you said yesterday?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. No. Actually we didn't have it. We just spent time on those premises. This is where our kitchen was for a certain period of time.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell me how far is Kozluk from Rocevici?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Seven kilometres.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: And this facility where you sometimes spent time, is it close to the factory Vitinka?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You said temporarily located.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: No. I asked you whether it's in the facility of Vitinka factory?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: In July 1995, when you went there as you explained, this facility had been abandoned --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I apologise to you, Mr. Nicholls.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I might be wrong. I think the interpreter is struggling a bit again is my feeling.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Yes, Mr. Zivanovic and Mr. Acimovic. You are both to blame.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Acimovic, before you came here you provided three statements to the Office of the Prosecutor; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Those statements were recorded, weren't they?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were recorded -- actually, the first two were. I'm not sure about the third one.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: At the time when you provided those statements, and again now, you did not feel threatened, you did not ask for any protective measures, in order to come and testify here or in order to provide your statements to the Tribunal; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: After that, did you have an occasion to look at the transcripts of those statements or to hear the recordings played back to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. I had such an occasion.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct if I told you that every time you gave a statement, each of those statements, new statements, contained something that you hadn't said in your previous statement?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is your view of the things.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: And you don't agree with that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I provided my statement based on what I remembered.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: In other words, whenever you remembered something new, then in your subsequent statement you added that to your previous statement, is that what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: In your first statement, provided in 2001, you never mentioned that you had met with Vujadin Popovic one day after the prisoners had been brought to Rocevic, and that he had asked you to assign people to execute these prisoners, that he had put pressure on you and so on and so forth, that he had threatened you, cursed you, sweared, am I right in thinking and saying that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was never put a question to be able to answer in that particular way, as far as I can remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, please, at the time you did not talk about that because a question was not put to you and you believe that the investigators were not interested in that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, not that they were not interested, but they simply did not jog my memory in that sense. They didn't mention anything to entice me to provide such an answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Are you saying that it simply didn't cross your mind when you were providing that statement and they never reminded you of such a detail?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: In the second interview, they did ask you this, and they also asked you how come you had not mentioned the thing that you were mentioning then in your first statement, that is that you had come across Popovic in the school or around the school, that he had put pressure on you, that he ordered you to allocate people to execute the prisoners, that he cursed you and swore, and your answer was more or less the same, in that second interview. However, the question that the investigators put to you at the time is something that is really striking and if you want me to, I can read the question that was put to you at the time back to you or I can give it to you to read it yourself. They first asked you whether you knew anything about a large number of prisoners that had been brought to the area of responsibility of the brigade, and then they explained to you and they asked you whether you could provide some more detail about those prisoners?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: And that is exactly what I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: But you never mentioned Popovic, the pressures put to you, the alleged request that you should assign people to execute these people and so on and so forth?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We spoke about the prisoners.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: In other words, that conversation with Popovic did not have anything to do with the prisoners?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not have the impression that I was supposed to talk about that, and it never occurred to me. I just did not think about that. I just focused on the questions that were put to me and I just made sure that I answered them. Given the fact that this had happened in 1995 and my first statement was provided maybe six or seven years later, I had to focus very hard on the questions and the answers that I was going to give.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: In other words, this encounter with Popovic, his request to give you people to execute the prisoners and the rest of the things, those things just slipped your mind at that moment?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Precisely.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Acimovic, now, when you're here, you've had interviews with the Prosecutor and you have provided them with some new information that was not known before, i.e., that you never mentioned in any of the three statements that you provided previously. Just, for example, let me mention a few things that you never mentioned in your second statement, even after your memory had been jogged. For example, you never stated in your statement that under the alleged Popovic's pressure you went to the school courtyard and asked for the volunteers to execute the prisoners. Is that another thing that simply slipped your mind?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not say anything to that effect. This is how I explained things: One of those individuals asked me what was going on, and then I said to them what I had been asked to do, what I had been requested to do, and that was all I said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Nicholls?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And the question has been asked and answered but just for the record I would object to that misstatement in the last question and what the witness has just said is precisely what he said on his direct examination, not what was put to him that he said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, what's your comment on that, Mr. Zivanovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the gist of my question is not the exact wording of what the witness said. The gist of my question is that the witness never said it before. This is the essence of my question. The witness never mentioned this detail before. That's why I'm putting this question to him and my question to him is precisely this:

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: How come you never mentioned this before?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I really can't answer your question. Not that I don't want to. I simply can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: You don't remember why you didn't mention it in any of your three interviews?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, precisely. You can't remember every detail, every tiny detail of every situation. I've already told you how long ago this happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. On that occasion, you also didn't say that you had asked from Popovic for people to be evacuated from Rocevic and then he called the brigade and asked for some vehicles?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Could you please repeat that question?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: On what occasion is the question that I have.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, Mr. Zivanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] First of all, the witness said it on page 55, line 17 of the LiveNote.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: In other words, it's still not clear in my mind either. If I understood Mr. Nicholls correctly, he was referring specifically to your question which was: "You don't remember why you didn't mention it in any of your three interviews?" "Yes, precisely. You can't remember every detail," et cetera. And then you said, "Yes. On that occasion you also didn't say that you had asked from Popovic for people to be evacuated ..." Which occasion? Because even from what you repeated, it's still not clear in my mind and the witness seems to have understood, and you seem to have understood his testimony here basically which I don't think is the case. I may be wrong but I --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: In none of your three statements did you mention that you asked from Popovic to evacuate these people and that after that Popovic called the brigade and asked for the lorries to be sent.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You should read my statements more carefully and you will find the answer to that question, my answer to what you're asking me now. I said, I believe I did, that I asked for these people to be evacuated, to be returned to wherever they had come from, because a disaster would take place, that some of the units might be tempted to leave their positions and so on and so forth.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Very well, then. Would you agree with me when I say that on any of the -- in any of the statements did you mention any of the names that you mentioned here in the courtroom?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I would agree.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: You also forgot them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: But you did not want to mention their names to the Prosecutor's Office?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: If I hadn't wanted to, I would not have mentioned them now.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: But in your three interviews, you didn't want to mention them, you remembered them but you didn't want to mention their names?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's not correct. You're not right.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Did you mention them in your first three interviews?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Line 7, 8 and 9 on page 30 are not clear. In any case, I think one could understand them. Let's proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Acimovic, tell me, please, can you actually give me the reasons why you never mentioned the names of these people before?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I've explained the reasons to the Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: You're not going to do the same for us, are you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not that I don't want to. I can do that. I told the Prosecutor--

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Your Honours, maybe we should go into private session. I don't know exactly what's coming.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Do you agree, Mr. Zivanovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I agree.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's go into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: At the request of Mr. Zivanovic, we are having a break now, and it will be of 25 minutes duration. That covers the redaction sufficiently? Okay? 25 minutes starting from now. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Zivanovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Acimovic, let us begin with your first statement and your other previous statements, about your arrival in Rocevici, in those days when the prisoners were there. Can you please first tell me how did you arrive at Rocevici?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In a car.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Was that a passenger car?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: After your arrival in Rocevici and until the president of the local commune and the priest came to see you, how long was it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I suppose about 30 minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: You and the president of the local commune and the priest went to the school?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: How long did it take you to get there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We drove in a car and it took a couple of minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: How far is your house from the school?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: About 400 to 500 to 600 metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Were you in the same car?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't think we were.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Acimovic, I have information that at that time, you talked to the men who were guarding the prisoners and that on that occasion you were alone. In other words, that you alone approached these soldiers without the priest and without the president of the local commune.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is the information you have.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. That is precisely what I said. Only tell me if that is true.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: I have another information that after you talked to these soldiers and this conversation lasted only a couple of minutes, you said that jerrycans with water will be provided and that these soldiers would be exchanged. In other words, this is what the soldiers told you, that these POWs were going to be exchanged; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: After that, as you said, you went to Kozluk?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: To make a telephone call?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: I put it to you that this is not true because in the log of the duty officer, which is an unofficial document, there is no entry with relation to any of the calls that you made. Do you know anything about that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is what you claim. This is what you are saying.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Exactly.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: So what do you want me to tell you?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Whether it's true or not.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You said that I was not telling the truth.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: So you have finished.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: You claim that you called the duty officer from Kozluk?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell me why didn't you do that from Rocevici?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Because at the time I didn't have a telephone available, an induction telephone available, not a civilian one but an induction telephone. There was one induction telephone in Kozluk on those premises that I mentioned before.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Does that mean that it was impossible to call the brigade from Rocevici via a regular phone?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: But you nevertheless decided to go to Kozluk?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think I was headed for my unit and on the way there, I made this call, because I didn't want to wait because this telephone was handy before I got to Malesic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: In other words, your original idea was first to go to Malesici?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, my first idea was to call the brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: From Malesici?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: From Kozluk.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: I understood you that you were on your way to Malesici, you just dropped by in Kozluk?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: My intention was to call the brigade as soon as possible, and that is what I did, and I did that from Kozluk for your information.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: You are saying that then you talked to Vujadin Popovic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: You said that you told him on that occasion that the men guarding the prisoners were under the influence of drugs or alcohol, that they were behaving erratically?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Acimovic, this applies more to you now than to Mr. Zivanovic. Please allow Mr. Zivanovic to finish his question and allow also a short pause after that so that we receive interpretation before you start giving your answer. You're trying to answer his questions before he has even finished them. So please calm down and take my advice, allow this short pause before you give your answer. Thank you. Yes, go ahead, Mr. Zivanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: You were then given an explanation that these prisoners would be exchanged on the following day?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: As I understand, this calmed you down to a certain extent and for that reason you went back to Kozluk -- no, I apologise -- to Rocevic, in order to convey this again to the president of the local commune and the priest?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: And they accepted that, that kind of explanation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I just relayed information to them.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: After that, you went to Malesic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, please, in what way did you, the president of the local commune and the priest were calmed down after receiving this information that on the following day the prisoners were going to be exchanged, since you knew that these men allegedly guarding the prisoners were to remain in the village and these people were behaving erratically, doing all sorts of things, they wounded a woman according to you? How could that possibly have calmed you, the priest, the president of the local commune and the whole village?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Didn't I tell you that we tried to convince the soldiers guarding the prisoners to give them water or to give permission for water to be given to the prisoners and everything else that they had asked for in order to calm those people down? They were in the gym. After these lengthy process of persuasion which lasted for about half an hour, I said that they accepted that, and I explained how they accepted for water to be given to them, and this I suppose had some effect on people getting calm. I also believed that this information was important and crucial, saying that those men were going to be exchanged the following day and that the killing would not -- the killing of the prisoners would not continue, and the things of that nature, and I believe that to be crucial information for the residents of that village.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: That was crucial information, as far as prisoners were concerned. What about the local residents? They had to stay there overnight. Your family, the families of your soldiers, had to spend the night with people who were armed, who were shooting, who wounded this woman. How could you become calm in view of that and leave that area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. I became calm.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Nicholls?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I may be wrong but I think it's exactly the same question pretty much that he answered about how after they had this discussion about the water everybody calmed down a little bit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think so too but Mr. Zivanovic might not agree with that. Let's proceed, Mr. Zivanovic. Let's proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: I've noticed in the transcript that it hasn't been recorded about the -- your facility of your battalion in Kozluk. Was it close to the Vitinka factory?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You assert that you informed your two colleagues, Mitar Lazarevic and Vujo Lazarevic, about all this?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. There may have been someone else, but -- from among my colleagues but I don't remember. That is why I mentioned their names specifically.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: You also mentioned a telegram that you received that night.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: You cannot recall who signed the telegram, as you said?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: You sent a reply, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I beg your pardon?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: You did send a reply to this telegram?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: You also don't know who it was addressed to?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We sent it back to the one who sent it to us, or to the duty operations officer.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Acimovic, I admit that I find it a little bit strange that you cannot remember who wrote and sent this telegram to you, in which you were requested to do something that probably nobody asked you to do the same thing during the war. Am I right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think I explained that in my previous statements quite sufficiently.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: I am under the impression, and correct me if I'm wrong, that by giving that reply, you were trying to protect someone.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Absolutely not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Again, Mr. Acimovic, please allow Mr. Zivanovic to finish his question and then also a brief pause so that we get the interpretation before you start giving your answer. Otherwise, it can happen that you will be answering in your own language and the interpreter -- while the interpreters are still translating to us what Mr. Zivanovic is saying. Yes, Mr. Zivanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: At the time when you gave this statement, you were aware that there were proceedings being conducted against Dragan Obrenovic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: You were in contact with his Defence team?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes. I had contacts with all Defence teams.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes. I'm talking about that particular period when you made those statements, that was in 2001 and 2002. Were you in touch with the Defence of Dragan Obrenovic at the time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. I said yes, I did, at their initiative.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Did you tell that to the investigators? Did they ask you about it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, I told them.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Do you remember when did you tell them that, on the first or the second or the third occasion?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I honestly cannot remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: I'll try to remind you. Did you say that when you were informed that you had been given a status of suspect? That was your last interview with the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: I have information that prior to Dragan Obrenovic's arrest, he had meetings with various people from the Zvornik Brigade, at which it was agreed what to say should they be asked questions by the Prosecution. Did you attend any of those meetings?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I didn't attend a single of those meetings with Obrenovic. Neither did I have any contact with him regarding this matter, at any time.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Did you have meetings with someone else?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I told you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: You assert that on that night, when you received the telegram, and generally during that day, you were unable to communicate with Dragan Obrenovic via the duty officer?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: At the time, Dragan Obrenovic was in command of the brigade and he was your immediate superior and I put it to you that you had direct communication line with him; am I right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, not at the time. In that period, but I don't know which period we are talking about. Earlier on, I had a line of communication with him but I could not communicate to him about the events that we are talking about.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: When was your line of communication between you and Obrenovic interrupted?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Can you specify what you mean? Can you be more specific when you say this direct line of communication? What do you mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: I would like to you clarify your previous answer. In your previous answer you stated, "Not at that time, at that time I did not have a direct line of communication."

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: "In that period, but I don't know what period you are talking about. Earlier on, I did have a line of communication with him but I could not communicate to him about the events that we are talking about."

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: All this time you are trying to play games of words with me. Let me try to explain some things to you. Every brigade commander and every Chief of Staff have very clear lines with the subordinate units, and I really don't understand what you are not clear about in that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: I'm absolutely very clear on everything, and this is what I am saying, that you had a direct line of communication with Obrenovic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: All the time.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is what you claim. This is your opinion and your view.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: And you're saying that you could not establish communication through the duty operations officer, through the radio?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You're right.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: And what about courier?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. That was not available to me because I didn't know where the courier was at the time. If I had known where he was, I would have probably sent him there.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Are you saying that the brigade didn't know either where the courier was either?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I'm not saying that. I can't say that. This is the answer I was given, and I have related it to you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Did you send a courier to the brigade for the duty operations officer to tell him where the courier was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Why would I send a courier to the brigade? I could communicate with the brigade. I was in communication with the brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: For the duty operations officer to tell me -- to tell him where Obrenovic was. Maybe he could have conveyed your message.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Why would the duty operations officer have told my courier where Obrenovic was and he would not have told me on several occasions that I tried to elicit that information from him?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: It arises from that, that the duty operations officer did not know where Obrenovic was.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I can't confirm that. He told me that he didn't know where he was, that he wasn't available, that he was in the field, and that he wasn't available. This is what the duty operations officer told me.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: But you don't know who the duty operations officer was?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: The interpreters are really doing a wonderful job with the difficulties that you are creating for them. I would hate to be in their position. Please slow down, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Acimovic, I'm putting it to you that you did not receive any telegrams from the brigade at the time and especially not a telegram with such content, requesting you to allocate people for the execution, and I am basing this on the fact that such a telegram was not registered anywhere.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You can put anything to -- you want to me, and I'm not interested the least bit in what you are putting to me because I'm telling the truth.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: You don't know where the telegram that you received can be found?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: I'm also putting to you that you never received an order either from the duty operations officer or in a telegram or from Vujadin Popovic to allocate men for the execution.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I've already told you: You can put anything you want to me. I'm not interested in that at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: If you had received an order of that sort, and you knew that it was illegal, why didn't you report that to your commander then?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Did I not tell you that I could not get in touch with either the commander or the Chief of Staff?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Until when?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: During that night and during the following day, I'm sure I couldn't. And I don't know exactly when after that the Chief of Staff returned to the brigade. I can't tell you when he returned to the brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: But I'm sure that you had an opportunity after that to report that to your commander?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not have an opportunity to discuss that matter at all. I reported that to the duty operations officer, and that was more than enough. The duty officer in the brigade got my report.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: And you believed that the commander should not have been informed about such an order that was against the law and that's why you didn't inform him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not that he should not have been informed. He was not there, and it was more than enough for the duty operations officer in the brigade to be briefed about such an order, and I believe that it was his duty to inform the commander or the Chief of Staff at their first opportunity.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we go to private session, please, Your Honours, just for a brief moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Certainly, Mr. Zivanovic. Let's go into private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And if either of you are at the point of mentioning any names that we haven't been mentioning in public session, then alert us immediately so that we go into private session. Yes, Mr. Zivanovic. We are in open session now.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Acimovic, you also couldn't remember who received that telegram?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's true.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: You can't remember --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Just a moment, please. Who received the telegram you're saying? I said in my previous statements that I believe that in the course of that night, the duty officer in the battalion command was Mitar Lazarevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Do you remember who decoded the telegram?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was not there at the moment when the telegram was decoded actually, I was asleep. They only woke me up once the telegram had been decoded and it arrived at my desk already decoded, when I came downstairs.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Do you remember who sent your reply?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I believe it was the duty operations officer as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment before you proceed. In your system at the time, was decoding a privileged matter? In other words, was there a specific person assigned to decoding messages or could anyone present there do it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think that every battalion command had a table for decoding of telegrams that were sent within that context and I believe that this could be found in the duty operations officer's room.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: My question is: Would the duty officer on duty at any time a message comes in be able or be able to decode that message or does he -- would he have to hand it over to a person tasked with the decoding procedure?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can't answer your question because in practice we received very few coded telegrams. I'm not sure whether the duty officer decoded the telegram himself or maybe he did it together with somebody else. It is possible that somebody assisted him, but I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Back to you, Mr. Zivanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: In your previous statements and again here, you have stated that upon the receipt of this telegram you didn't call the duty officer in the brigade in order to check the accuracy of the telegram; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Nicholls?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Again, just to be clear for the record. There were two telegrams. I don't know exactly -- maybe he said the first one, I'm not sure though, it's not clear on the record which telegram my friend is asking questions about.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That's a legitimate observation. Perhaps you can address this, Mr. Zivanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'll try and be more precise.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: In your previous statements you have stated that you didn't call the duty officer either after the first or the second telegram in order to check their accuracy; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I really can't remember. I don't remember at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please move into private session again, Your Honours?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Let's do that, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We are in open session now.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: In your previous statements, you mentioned that in front of you Popovic requested two men to be sent to him from the brigade. This time, you said that he only asked for one of the two.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Maybe it was not interpreted properly, if that is what you heard. I always maintained that he wanted one of the two. That is literally what he said.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: In your previous statements, the Prosecutor asked you, inter alia, if you had seen any trucks arriving at Rocevici.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment before you answer. Yes, Mr. Nicholls?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I'd like a page reference from my friend please about the previous statement because I'm looking at page 30 of the 2002 interview and his answer on this issue is, "He said send me one of the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment. You shouldn't be saying this in the witness's presence.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I apologise. Then I just ask for a page reference.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Just ask for a page reference and you would be able to follow.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: It is page 30 of his interview from -- no, no, no, no, just a moment. It is second interview, his second interview, page 30.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So that's the same one you had in mind, Mr. Nicholls? Or is it a different one?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: It may be. I haven't had time but what I have on page 30 in English does not reflect what was put to the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Right. Let's make sure we are talking of the same section first. Okay? Mr. Zivanovic is suggesting that this comes from page 30 of the second interview, and you had referred to page 30 of the 2002 interview.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: That's the same interview and I'm looking at lines 5 to 6. It's ERN L0069717 that I'm referring to. And that should be at about page 29, lines 19 to 21 of the B/C/S version.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: There seems to be disagreement between you as to the way that you are putting your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: No, I'll withdraw my question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, both of you. Go ahead, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Acimovic, I'm going to show you the records of attendance of personnel that I mentioned before. I'm going to ask you just to tell me if you remember that. Do you remember this document? It's a document -- maybe we can use an ELMO because I can't give you the precise number. Maybe it will be easier for you if you look to the right. I think you can see it there better. Now you also have it on your monitor. What I wanted to ask you is this regarding this -- these records: Can you tell me, please, do you remember seeing this record?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Partly.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: I think this shouldn't be broadcast. That would be advisable.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Is there a reason why you wouldn't like it to be broadcast? Okay. I can understand the reason. All right. So we block the broadcasting for the same reasons as before. And we go into private session.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. The reason for it not to be broadcast is because some of potential witnesses may be on this list. That's the only reason.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Are you going to refer to names specifically?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, I'm not, no. I'm not going to mention any names. That is -- but I just ask for it not to be broadcast anyway.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Okay. Then we can proceed in open session but we'll block that part where it was broadcast in any case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Go ahead, Mr. Zivanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Do you remember these records?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. I didn't keep these records.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know who did?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Probably the general affairs desk officer.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Was that the aforementioned Mr. Mitar Lazarevic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I suppose so.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Then you don't know if these records were forwarded to the brigade command. Was it sent to someone, to the brigade command?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I'm not sure but I think this is just a formality. I didn't pay any attention at all to these matters at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: It says here that this is the record of the presence of personnel in the command involved in combat operations. You were not interested in that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not that I wasn't interested in that, but we had our assignments and our tasks given to each individual listed here, and this is where particular attention was paid, and I think that this was done by the general affairs desk officer. It even says here that there is a man called Stevo Savic and some other names, but I noticed Stevo Savic who at the time was demobilised, which means that this is not a valid document. So actually you can see here -- yes, these boxes are empty, blank.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: At any rate, you maintain that you never saw this, never checked this?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I never checked this kind of documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: You would recall -- I apologise. Just give me a second to find it -- your statement -- your third statement given to the Prosecution, or not -- rather, not the statement but the interview that you had with the Prosecutor, that was your last interview before your coming here and it took place on the 29th of October 2002?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Did you say the second one?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: 29th of October 2002?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: And what kind of statement are you referring to, the first or second one?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: This was just an information report. We are not talking about the interviews that you had and which were audio recorded.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Again, please slow down. Yes, Mr. Nicholls?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I don't know if my friend is done with the document but I don't think it's anywhere in the record what the 65 ter number was or what we were looking at.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: It's on the list, it was put in e-court.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The document was 65 ter number 312, Prosecution document.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: We are talking about this information report compiled on the 29th of October 2002. In this report, you said, among other things, that you accepted the fact that you will have to testify and that you wouldn't be very happy to do that because the accused in that case were your former war comrades.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: And by that, you meant Mr. Obrenovic as well?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please repeat his answer?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Acimovic, the interpreters couldn't hear your answer because you gave it while they were still translating to us. Can you repeat it, please?
